subject: Math
prompt: Which of the following expressions is equivalent to $(3-root(x^{2}) \times sqrt(x^{3}))/(\frac{x^{7}}{6})$ for $x>0$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. Rewriting the radicals using fractional exponents gives $\frac{x^{\frac{2}{3}} \cdot x^{\frac{3}{2}}}{x^{\frac{7}{6}}}$. Adding the exponents in the numerator: $\frac{2}{3}+\frac{3}{2}=\frac{4}{6}+\frac{9}{6}=\frac{13}{6}$. Then subtracting the denominator exponent: $\frac{13}{6}-\frac{7}{6}=\frac{6}{6}=1$. Therefore the expression simplifies to $x^{1}=x$.
